Modern Gujarati commercial theatre

Following the development of amateur and literary theatre, Gujarati commercial theatre underwent substantial changes during the second half of the 20th century.

New professional groups presented original Gujarati plays, adaptations of foreign dramas and productions concerned with contemporary social relationships. These developments helped modern Gujarati theatre reach audiences beyond the older repertoire of mythological and historical musical plays.

Pravin Joshi

Pravin Joshi was a leading actor and director of modern Gujarati theatre during the 1960s and 1970s. He was closely associated with the Indian National Theatre (INT) in Bombay.

His contribution was particularly important in modern commercial theatre. He combined popular entertainment with literary and experimental productions, bringing both original Gujarati writing and international dramatic works to the stage.

Joshi worked with playwrights including Madhu Rye, Ramji Vania and Sitanshu Yashashchandra. His wife, the actress Sarita Joshi, appeared alongside him in several successful productions.

Santu Rangili and Kumarni Agashi

These two plays illustrate an important distinction in the work of Madhu Rye and Pravin Joshi.

Santu Rangili was a Gujarati adaptation of George Bernard Shaw's Pygmalion, a play concerned with language, social class and identity. Madhu Rye was responsible for the Gujarati adaptation, while Pravin Joshi directed and performed in its theatrical production.

Kumarni Agashi, by contrast, was an original Gujarati play written by Madhu Rye and directed by Pravin Joshi. Both works contributed to the reputation of modern Gujarati theatre, but only the former is an adaptation of Pygmalion.

Moti Verana Chowkma

Moti Verana Chowkma demonstrates Pravin Joshi's engagement with indigenous theatrical traditions. Written by Ramji Vania, it drew upon Bhavai. Its production shows that modern commercial theatre could incorporate both international dramatic works and regional folk traditions.

Pravin Joshi should primarily be remembered as the actor-director associated with Indian National Theatre and its major modern productions. A play directed by him was not necessarily written or originally conceived by him.

Understanding the continuity of Gujarati theatre

The history of Gujarati Rangbhumi can be understood through four broad developments: the indigenous Bhavai tradition, the emergence of the Parsi-influenced urban stage, the expansion of Gujarati-owned professional theatre companies and the growth of modern amateur, literary and commercial theatre.

These developments overlapped. Asait Thakar represents the folk foundation; Dalpatram and Ranchhodbhai Dave represent early dramatic writing and organised theatre; Mulani and Prabhulal Dwivedi represent the prominent professional playwrights; Chandravadan Mehta represents the modern amateur and literary movement; and Pravin Joshi represents the renewal of modern commercial theatre.

The revival of Bhavai through Mena Gurjari, Jasma Odan and Moti Verana Chowkma demonstrates that indigenous theatrical traditions continued to influence modern Gujarati drama.

Prelims focus

  • Pravin Joshi: Indian National Theatre, Bombay.
  • Santu Rangili: Madhu Rye; adaptation of Shaw's Pygmalion.
  • Kumarni Agashi: original Gujarati play by Madhu Rye.
  • Moti Verana Chowkma: Ramji Vania; Bhavai influence.
  • Vaishakhi Koyal: Sitanshu Yashashchandra.
  • Trap: Pravin Joshi directed both Santu Rangili and Kumarni Agashi, but their Gujarati writer was Madhu Rye.
